clue.text: Lion-tamer could be put out of business by industrial action

definitions.text: Lion-tamer could be put out of business by industrial action

parts.words: Lion-tamer could be put out of business by industrial action
parts.note: read literally, a big cat on the loose and out of control would leave a circus performer with nothing to do; really it is a sudden unofficial walkout

explanation.surface: A circus performer fears losing work because of a union dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Industrial action' looks like the whole meaning, but the joke is in reading the first word of the answer as a feral feline.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial stoppage called by workers without union approval is the industrial action meant.

parts.note: a fight won by slowly grinding the enemy down, wearing being both tiring and abrading

explanation.surface: A dispute that grinds on and exhausts everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign of steady attrition defeats the enemy by gradual exhaustion of men and materiel.

parts.note: looks like a man arriving north of the border; landed here means owning an estate

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives by plane or boat in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish landowner with an estate is known by this title.

clue.text: Tidying after it has been raining?

explanation.surface: Someone tidies the garden once the shower has stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidying is putting things in order; after rain the weather improves as the clouds disperse.

indicators.note: disrupted tells us the letters of the word parties are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A vagrant breaks up some gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk wearily, the same as to trudge about.

clue.text: Where in France tunes composed outside are weak and unconvincing

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged tunes go around the French word
composed suggests the letters of tunes are arranged afresh, as music is

parts.note: ou is French for where

explanation.surface: Somewhere in France, music is written that lacks strength and persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' gives TENUS from the anagram, and 'outside' wraps it round the French word, which sits between the first four letters and the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A flimsy argument is thin and lacks substance, slight and insubstantial.

clue.text: Bisect, so to speak, to within

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the phrase for bisect is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to bisect is to cut in two

explanation.surface: A geometry instruction to halve something.
explanation.walkthrough: To bisect is to cut 'in two', which when spoken matches the preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means moving to a position inside something.

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of cautioned are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was given a warning regarding their coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling and instruction are a form of training.

parts.note: a coordinator is someone who organises
a purse is prize money, as in boxing

explanation.surface: An event coordinator holds up a trophy box.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet with many compartments for cards and cash is a kind of container.

clue.text: Rouse one in prison and cause a disturbance

parts.note: to rouse is to raise or stir up

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Waking a jailed inmate causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN is American slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an uproar, as Cain the biblical troublemaker suggests.

clue.text: Squarer egghead entering city dropped round at the end

indicators.note: entering says the head letter of egg goes inside the shortened city
dropped says the ring-shaped letter is lost from the end of the city

parts.note: Truro is the cathedral city of Cornwall
O is round in shape
the head, or first letter, of egg

explanation.surface: An intellectual comes into town after a ring went missing at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: TRURO is Cornwall's city, in south-west England; 'dropped round at the end' removes its final O, giving TRUR, and E goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Squarer, as in more level or more honest, means more accurate or straighter.

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of fared have gone badly wrong and are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some electrical gadget performed very poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding control that adjusts sound or light levels is an electrical device.

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for left goes inside the word for big sum

parts.note: a pot is a large sum of money

explanation.surface: A lot of money is left in the scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or plot is a secret plan.

clue.text: A small party back in Wales

indicators.note: back tells us the letters of a and the short party name are read in reverse

parts.note: Lab is the short form of the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A minor political group returns to Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: BALA is a small town and lake in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The town and its lake are located in Gwynedd, a Welsh county.

parts.note: flight here is a set of steps, not an escape; domestic staff used hidden steps at the rear of a house

explanation.surface: Household staff slip away in a clandestine escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear steps used by domestic staff in grand houses, out of sight of the family.

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for right is turned around

parts.note: an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A footballer playing at right-back beats an opponent despite being light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-back' looks like a football position, but it splits into RT reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat soundly is to defeat decisively.

clue.text: Not even this man is a member of society

parts.note: an odd number is not even
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: This man is uneven but belongs to society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society, a mutual-aid organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone belonging to the Oddfellows, a fraternal friendly society.

clue.text: Translated his wail into a foreign language

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters of his wail are converted into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone's cry of anguish is rendered into another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bantu tongue widely spoken in East Africa is a foreign language to English speakers.

explanation.surface: A researcher has doubts again about their work in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fieldwork' suggests research outdoors, but it means a temporary earthwork fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fresh uncertainty is to doubt again; a small fort built in the field is a fieldwork.

parts.note: looks like someone departing in a fury or autumn bonfires; really dried leaves smoked in a pipe or cigarette

explanation.surface: Autumn foliage is set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried plant leaves smoked in cigarettes and pipes.

parts.note: to ask is to enquire about something
CE is the Church of England, the Establishment

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a business in a roundabout way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is often called the Establishment in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking sideways at something, with suspicion, is to look at it obliquely.

clue.text: See nameless woman performing and find it daunting

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters act out a new arrangement
nameless says the abbreviation for name is dropped from the word woman

explanation.surface: Watching an anonymous female performer proves intimidating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' takes N (name) from WOMAN, leaving WOMA; 'performing' then rearranges SEE and WOMA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inspiring awe and dread is formidable.

indicators.note: enter says the letter I goes inside the word for three times

parts.note: ter is Latin for three times, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone goes in thrice.
explanation.walkthrough: TER, Latin for thrice, appears in medical prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, a rank in a series.

clue.text: Talented bachelor getting in some drink

indicators.note: getting in says the abbreviation for bachelor goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of drink

explanation.surface: A gifted single man buys a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted and skilful people are capable.

parts.note: a card of the suit that beats all others, and also the final call of a horn on Judgment Day

explanation.surface: Which card remains for the final play?
explanation.definitionFit: A card of the suit ranking above the rest, and the last call sounded at the end of the world.

clue.text: Some consult Raymond who's an extremist

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people consult Raymond, who holds radical views.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with radical views in politics or religion is a zealot.

indicators.note: not says the little word in is removed from the name

parts.note: Ingrid is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lady is absent from the network.
explanation.definitionFit: The national electricity system is a network of cables and stations.

indicators.note: did not start says the first letter of the heater is lost

parts.note: a boiler heats water

explanation.surface: A tanker's water heating system failed to fire up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that carries oil is a tanker.

clue.text: Person responsible for a series of notes

definitions.text: Person responsible for a series of notes

parts.words: Person responsible for a series of notes
parts.note: suggests a writer of memos or banker; really a singer in a church choir producing musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone is in charge of a run of memos.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a church choir sings a sequence of musical notes.

parts.note: looks like a gaping hole; really a vast empty stretch of countryside

explanation.surface: A large chasm opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad untamed countryside is an expansive empty area.
